summary: Iteration 4 — verified deck.gl HexagonLayer addition to Map Intelligence + pako regression fix. All requested acceptance criteria pass: (1) Third button [data-testid='layer-hex3d'] renders alongside 'layer-cases' and 'layer-predictions'. (2) Clicking it mounts [data-testid='deck-hex-view'] which contains 1 WebGL <canvas> with real extruded 3D hexagons over Karnataka (verified visually — cyan/emerald/amber/orange/red/crimson bins, OSM basemap desaturated + tinted). (3) Sliders [data-testid='deck-radius'] (6000→12000) and [data-testid='deck-elevation'] (220→400) update in real time; labels reflect '6.0 km' and '×220'. (4) Switching back to 'layer-cases' unmounts deck-hex-view (count=0) and remounts Leaflet (.leaflet-container count=1); 'layer-predictions' also renders Leaflet. (5) REGRESSION CLEAN: zero 'Cannot find pako.esm.mjs' errors in console or frontend supervisor logs after last successful compile. Regression sweep across /dashboard, /cases, /analytics, /predictions, /reports, /users, /audit — all load without page errors.

issues: Initial view state (lng=76.0, lat=14.8, pitch=52°, bearing=12°) causes the hex column cluster to appear visually offset from the Karnataka landmass labels on the OSM basemap (hexes sit to the east/over the sea/Tamil Nadu edge in default viewport). Recentering to ~(lng=76.5, lat=15.3) or reducing bearing would align the extrusions over the actual state. Not a bug — 3D perspective + high pitch amplifies parallax.

Console warning 'THREE.WARNING: Multiple instances of Three.js being imported' repeats. Likely because deck.gl bundles its own three plus another dep (react-globe or similar) also imports three. Non-blocking but worth deduping via webpack resolve.alias 'three'.

action_items: (LOW) Nudge DeckHexView INITIAL_VIEW_STATE to better center Karnataka (e.g., longitude≈76.5, latitude≈15.3, pitch≈45, bearing≈0) so the 3D column cluster overlays the state rather than drifting east.
(LOW) Dedupe 'three' via webpack resolve.alias to silence the 'Multiple instances of Three.js' console warning.
critical_code_review_comments: DeckHexView.jsx correctly memoises layers with the right updateTriggers (radius, elevationScale). Good.

TileLayer BitmapLayer bounds destructuring `boundingBox[0][0]..[1][1]` assumes the older tuple format. On recent @deck.gl/geo-layers (>=9), tile.boundingBox may be `[[west,south],[east,north]]` — appears correct here (worked in screenshot), but pin the deck.gl version in package.json to avoid future breakage.

craco.config.js filter strips source-map-loader from BOTH oneOf and top-level rules. Effective, but could be tighter by only excluding node_modules rather than removing the loader entirely — devs lose source-maps for app code too. Consider `enforce: 'pre'` rule with `exclude: /node_modules/` instead of filter-out.

MapIntel.jsx: DeckHexView is fed the same `points` array used by Leaflet CircleMarker — good reuse. But there's no loading/error state for the /map/hotspots fetch — empty array silently renders zero hexagons.
Bearing=12 in INITIAL_VIEW_STATE gives an off-axis view that visually misaligns with basemap labels; consider bearing=0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: DeckHexView renders correctly with WebGL canvas and functional sliders. Pako ESM error resolved via craco source-map-loader filter. Only cosmetic follow-ups: recenter initial view + dedupe three.js. All other Namma Kavacha features from iteration 3 remain intact (dashboard, cases, analytics, network, predictions, reports, users, audit all loaded without page errors during regression sweep).
